meta.title: Xpanda: shell expansion, minus the shell
meta.description: Substitute variables in text with the parameter expansion you know from Bash, without running any code. A single binary for Linux and Windows, and a Rust crate.

hero.lede: Xpanda substitutes variables in text using the parameter expansion you already know from Bash. It does more than envsubst and never runs code like eval would. It ships as a single native binary for Linux and Windows, and as a Rust crate with zero dependencies.

demo.label: Live demo
demo.caption: Try it, everything runs in your browser
demo.hint: Try deleting HOST from the variables, or setting PORT=443.

fit.title: More than envsubst. Less than a template engine. Never eval.
fit.intro: Most config templating needs defaults, required values and a little string trimming. Xpanda covers that with syntax your team already reads, and it can't run a command no matter what ends up in the input.

envsubst.body: Substitutes $VAR and ${VAR}. No defaults, so a missing variable silently becomes an empty string.

xpanda.body: Defaults, alternatives, required values, length, indirection, substrings, case changes, glob trimming and replacement. Everything from POSIX and Bash expansion that makes sense outside a shell.

eval.body: Expands every form, including $(...) command substitution. Any template, or any value inside one, can run arbitrary commands.

patterns.title: Every form, evaluated live.
patterns.intro: Change the value of VAR and each result below is computed again. Glob patterns support *, ? and character classes.

usage.title: In your pipeline, or in your code.

cli.title: CLI
cli.body: Reads a file or standard input, writes to standard output or a file. Values come from the environment, a var file, flags or positional arguments.

comments.file: a var file, written to a new file

library.title: Library
library.body: One struct, one method. Build it with the variables you want available and call expand. Errors come back as a typed Error, never a panic.
